GALAH_rv_veto.provenance_degradation: used the fallback route GALAH_DR4_allstar_cloud (https://cloud.datacentral.org.au/teamdata/GALAH/public/GALAH_DR4/catalogs/galah_dr4_allstar_240705.fits) rather than the preferred GALAH_DR4_allstar_dc; no rv column: the instrumental-covariate veto on rv cannot run on this table; no fiber column: the instrumental-covariate veto on fiber cannot run on this table
GALAH_rv_veto.verdict: the GALAH_DR4_allstar_cloud FITS table carries no radial-velocity and no fibre column, so covariate_rate_veto could not be evaluated on either. pass_rv_rate / pass_fiber_rate are True for all 1341 candidates by default, not by test. The single largest candidate-carrying element in GALAH is K (the 7699 A resonance doublet, the exact line Weinberg et al. traced onto a telluric band at v_helio ~ -70 km/s), and that is precisely the veto that could not run.

analysis_4_cut_chain.selection_code: acquire.selection_mask: (teff>4000)&(teff<6000)&(logg>4.0)&(snr>40)&(fe_h>-1.0), all with isfinite(); no other row cut. apply_selection truncates to max_rows AFTER the selection.

truncation_verdict.verdict: NOT truncated. rows_in_file = 917,588 for GALAH is the full DR4 allstar row count and 733,901 for APOGEE is the full DR17 allStarLite row count; the 400,000-row cap is applied after the selection and 73,820 / 155,709 are both far below it, so it never bit. The 8.05% is the cool-dwarf/SNR/[Fe/H] selection doing exactly what it is specified to do.

pipeline_rv_flag_ratio.note: covariate_rate_veto uses 12 equal-population quantile bins over the full parent RV range. The Weinberg K/telluric feature is a ~10-20 km/s wide window; a 12-quantile binning of a +/-200 km/s distribution puts it inside a bin dominated by ordinary stars, so the measured ratio maxes out at 1.32 against a veto threshold of 5.0. The veto is not merely un-triggered, it is un-triggerable at this resolution: max attainable ratio is ~12 and only if every flag in the survey fell in one bin.

analysis_2b_galah.consequence: the identical test cannot be run for GALAH, whose K-carried candidates are 528/1341 = 39.4% of the candidate list. GALAH DR4 does publish rv_comp_1 / rv_galah in the allstar table; the cloud FITS route that was actually used resolved no rv column, so the strongest available veto on the single largest candidate-carrying element was silently skipped.

note_min_elements: SparseConfig dataclass default is 8; config/thresholds.yaml ships 12 and that is what the run used. 12 is used here.

headline.gaussian_null: With independent N(0,1) residuals and the real per-star element counts, 10^6 synthetic stars through the SHIPPED rules give 8 SPARSE (GALAH element set, 19.7 elements/star) and 3 SPARSE (APOGEE, 11.1 elements/star) per 10^6. Scaled to the surveys that is 0.59 and 0.41 expected sparse stars, against 1,341 and 3,173 observed.
headline.sparse_over_dense: Under pure Gaussian noise SPARSE OUTNUMBERS DENSE ~4:1, because DENSE needs >=3 elements simultaneously past 5 sigma. Every independent heavy-tailed model in the scan keeps sparse/dense >= 2.4. The observed ratios are 0.52 (GALAH) and 1.30 (APOGEE) -- DENSE is 5-8x more common relative to SPARSE than ANY independent per-element noise model can produce. The residuals are therefore not just heavy-tailed, they are CORRELATED ACROSS ELEMENTS, which is exactly what Weinberg et al. report (correlated groups Ca-Na-Al-K-Cr-Ce and Ni-V-Mn-Co). No independent-noise model, Gaussian or Student-t, reproduces the observed sparse/dense split.
headline.tail_heaviness: Matching the observed sparse RATE alone needs Student-t with dof ~7.3 (GALAH) and ~4.6 (APOGEE). Measuring the tail directly from the z_max distribution in the contrast table needs dof ~6.2 at z=4 falling to ~4.1 at z=12 (GALAH) and ~4.1 falling to ~3.5 (APOGEE): the required dof DECREASES with threshold, so the real residual tail is heavier than ANY single Student-t. dof ~3.5-4 has barely-finite variance -- that is a systematics-dominated error distribution, not a measurement one.

analysis_1c_sign_asymmetry.finding: The sign asymmetry is PER ELEMENT, not global. GALAH is 43.4% deficits overall, but that is a cancellation of element-locked populations: Y is 98.4% EXCESS (245/249), Cu 95.7% excess, Cr 94.3% excess, Ba 88.0% excess, while Al is 97.8% DEFICIT, O 95.3%, Zn 90.6%, Ca 88.0%, Mg 84.7%, Sc 80.0%. 10 of the 11 GALAH elements with >=20 candidates are locked to one sign at 80/20 or better, carrying 58.6% of the candidates; the one exception is K (40.2% deficit), the largest carrier, whose two-sidedness is itself consistent with a telluric that both eats the line and disturbs the local continuum. APOGEE is 92.5% deficits overall: Na 99.8% (1578/1581), V 99.1%, Cr 98.7%, Ti 88.5%, K 82.7% -- 5 locked elements carrying 87.6% of the candidates.
analysis_1c_sign_asymmetry.interpretation: A refining, debris-dumping or marker signature has no reason to pick a sign, and TAILINGS is sign-agnostic by construction; a genuine astrophysical population would also not have its sign determined by WHICH element carries it. An element-locked sign is the signature of a one-sided pipeline pathology: a line lost to a telluric, a bad pixel, a cosmic ray or bad continuum placement can only DEPRESS an abundance, while an unrecognised blend, a grid edge or a saturated core fitted on the flat part of the curve of growth can only INFLATE one. Each element sits on whichever side its own dominant failure mode pushes it. This is a per-element systematic, and it is independent evidence from the concentration argument.

conclusions: 1. CONCENTRATION: 74.1% of all 4,514 sparse candidates (3,343) are carried by few-line / measurement-floor-prone species. GALAH 84.8% (K 39.4%, Y 18.6%, Al 6.9%, Zn 4.8%); APOGEE 69.5% (Na 49.8%, K 7.1%, V 7.1%, O 4.7%). Stronger still, no element in either survey has a run-measured median residual width below 0.028 dex: all 25 GALAH and all 17 APOGEE species sit AT OR ABOVE the 0.03-0.06 dex Bedell few-line floor and NONE is near the ~0.01 dex well-measured floor. 97% (GALAH) and 100% (APOGEE) of candidates are carried by species wider than 0.03 dex. The z-score denominator is set by measurement systematics for every element, so the candidate population is a measurement floor, not a discovery.

2. SIGN: the candidates are sign-locked BY ELEMENT. 10 of 11 GALAH elements with >=20 candidates and 5 of 11 in APOGEE are >=80/20 one-signed, carrying 58.6% and 87.6% of the candidates respectively, and the sign is set by the element rather than by the star: GALAH Y is 98.4% EXCESS while Al is 97.8% DEFICIT; APOGEE Na is 99.8% deficit, V 99.1%, Cr 98.7%. Overall APOGEE is 92.5% deficits. A refining or marker signature has no preferred sign and TAILINGS is sign-agnostic by construction, so an element-locked sign is a per-element pipeline pathology -- line loss depresses an abundance, unrecognised blends and saturated cores inflate one -- not a population of anomalous stars.

3. RV/FIBRE: GALAH could not run the veto at all -- the FITS route used carries no rv and no fiber column, rv_flag_ratio and fiber_flag_ratio are 100% null for all 1,341 candidates, and pass_rv_rate/pass_fiber_rate are True by default rather than by test. GALAH's top element is K (528 candidates, 39.4%), the 7699 A resonance doublet, which is the exact Weinberg failure mode. On APOGEE, where the columns exist, the Weinberg signature IS PRESENT AND SIGNIFICANT: K-carried candidates are enhanced 2.98x in the a-priori -80 to -60 km/s window (p=1.2e-4), 4.03x over an (Fe/H, Teff)-matched control in -110 to -60 km/s (p=2.7e-10), and 28 of the 29 K anomalies in that window are DEFICITS -- a telluric eating the K line. The pipeline vetoed none of them, because covariate_rate_veto uses 12 equal-population quantile bins over the full +/-200 km/s range, which dilutes a ~20 km/s telluric window to a flag ratio of at most 1.32 against a veto threshold of 5.0. The veto is un-triggerable at that resolution.

4. NOISE MODEL: the Gaussian null predicts 0.59 (GALAH) and 0.41 (APOGEE) sparse stars; 1,341 and 3,173 are observed -- excesses of 2,271x and 7,718x. Matching the rate needs Student-t dof ~7.3 / ~4.6; matching the z_max distribution directly needs dof falling from ~6.2 to ~4.1 (GALAH) and ~4.1 to ~3.5 (APOGEE) as the threshold rises, so no single t fits. And no independent-noise model of any dof reproduces the observed sparse/dense ratio (0.52 and 1.30 observed vs >=2.4 for every model tested), so the residuals are element-correlated on top of being heavy-tailed.

5. CUT CHAIN: NOT truncated. GALAH rows_in_file = 917,588 (the full DR4 allstar row count) -> 73,820 after the Teff 4000-6000 / logg>4.0 / SNR>40 / [Fe/H]>-1 selection = 8.05%. APOGEE 733,901 (full DR17 allStarLite) -> 155,709 = 21.2% -> 137,047 after dedupe on star_id (18,662 duplicate rows). The 400,000-row cap is applied AFTER the selection and both survivors are far below it, so it never bit. The ~8% is the intended selection.
verdict.bottom_line: The 1.0% vetted rate (2,100/210,867), 55x Griffith et al. 2022, is the survey error model. Four independent lines of evidence converge: (a) 74.1% of candidates are carried by few-line species and every element in both surveys has a residual width at or above the Bedell few-line floor, none near the well-measured floor; (b) the candidates are sign-locked by element (58.6% of GALAH and 87.6% of APOGEE candidates carried by >=80/20 one-signed species), which no enrichment process produces; (c) a live Weinberg-type telluric artefact is demonstrable in APOGEE K at 4.0x over an (Fe/H, Teff)-matched control in the -110 to -60 km/s window (p=2.7e-10), with 28 of 29 of those anomalies being deficits, and the shipped covariate veto cannot catch it; and (d) the observed rate is 2,271x (GALAH) / 7,718x (APOGEE) the Gaussian null, needs a Student-t with dof ~3.5-7 to reproduce, and the sparse/dense ratio is unreachable by ANY independent per-element noise model. The z_flag=5.0 threshold sits at roughly the 1-in-300 point of the real dof~4 residual distribution, not the 1-in-3,000,000 point of a Gaussian one, which is the whole of the 55x.
